RECA-CA-R4-MLO-PROCESSOR-CONTRACTOR-001.question: A California DRE mortgage loan originator hires an independent contractor to process residential loans. Which credential authorizes the work?
RECA-CA-R4-MLO-PROCESSOR-CONTRACTOR-001.explanation: California Business and Professions Code 10166.03(c) requires an independent contractor who processes residential mortgage loans for an originator to obtain an MLO endorsement. Performing only processing tasks does not qualify the contractor for the employee exemption.

RENJ-NJ-REBATE-ADVERTISEMENT-TAX-NOTICE-.question: A New Jersey commission rebate ad advises buyers to consult a tax professional. What else must it disclose?
RENJ-NJ-REBATE-ADVERTISEMENT-TAX-NOTICE-.optionB: Buyer's duty to pay any applicable taxes
RENJ-NJ-REBATE-ADVERTISEMENT-TAX-NOTICE-.optionC: Buyer's tax year for the rebate
RENJ-NJ-REBATE-ADVERTISEMENT-TAX-NOTICE-.explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16b requires the ad to tell buyers they owe any applicable taxes and should consult a tax professional. Both notices must be conspicuous and in type at least as large as the ad text.

RETX-TXAGY-002.explanation: Texas Occupations Code 1101.558(c) exempts conversations about the property being shown at an open house. The lease exemption applies only to a residential lease shorter than one year when no sale is being considered.

REGA-GACLS-005.explanation: Georgia Code 44-1-16(a) requires a licensee asked about a death on the property to answer truthfully from personal knowledge. The licensee may withhold the answer if disclosure would violate a federal or state law, rule or regulation, including fair housing law.

REWA-WAAGY-004.explanation: RCW 18.86.030(1)(f) requires the broker to give a client the pamphlet as soon as reasonably practical and before the client signs a services agreement. An unrepresented party must receive it before signing an offer or as soon as reasonably practical.

RECA-CA-BUYER-004.question: A California listing agent gives an unrepresented visitor a tour at the seller's open house. What does the tour alone establish?
RECA-CA-BUYER-004.optionC: Buyer agency limited to that visit
RECA-CA-BUYER-004.explanation: Regulation 2906.2(c) allows a seller's agent to show the property on the seller's behalf. This act alone does not create an agency relationship with the visitor.

RECA-CA-R4-MLDS-EARLY-OBLIGATION-001.question: A broker receives a completed loan application Monday. The note will bind the borrower Tuesday. When is California's Mortgage Loan Disclosure Statement due?
RECA-CA-R4-MLDS-EARLY-OBLIGATION-001.optionD: By the next business day after signing
RECA-CA-R4-MLDS-EARLY-OBLIGATION-001.explanation: Business and Professions Code 10240 requires disclosure within three business days of the completed written application or before the borrower becomes obligated, whichever comes first. Here the borrower becomes obligated on Tuesday.

RECA-CA-R5-ASSIST-AD-PREPUBLICATION-001.question: An unlicensed California assistant designs a listing ad. Whose approval is required before it runs?
RECA-CA-R5-ASSIST-AD-PREPUBLICATION-001.explanation: DRE guidelines permit an assistant to design the ad. A broker or associate licensee must review and approve it before publication.

RECA-CA-R3-DRE-001.question: Someone negotiates California home sales for a fee without a license. What may DRE do after receiving a complaint?
RECA-CA-R3-DRE-001.optionA: Refer the case to the local trade association only
RECA-CA-R3-DRE-001.optionC: Wait for a buyer to obtain a civil judgment
RECA-CA-R3-DRE-001.optionD: Open a case once the negotiator applies for a license
RECA-CA-R3-DRE-001.explanation: DRE can investigate anyone performing acts that require a real estate license. Its jurisdiction includes people who never obtained a license.

RECA-CA-R3-FAIR-002.question: A California landlord charges a higher deposit solely because an applicant uses a housing voucher. The total meets the deposit cap. What rule applies?
RECA-CA-R3-FAIR-002.optionB: Deposit limits control if the policy is written
RECA-CA-R3-FAIR-002.optionC: Local voucher administrators set the deposit
RECA-CA-R3-FAIR-002.optionD: Equal base rent permits different security deposits
RECA-CA-R3-FAIR-002.explanation: California prohibits different rental terms because of a housing subsidy. Staying under the deposit cap does not justify charging voucher holders more.

RECA-CA-R3-ASSIST-001.question: A visitor asks an unlicensed California open-house assistant for a private tour and advice on offer terms. What may the assistant do?
RECA-CA-R3-ASSIST-001.optionA: Conduct the tour with the owner present
RECA-CA-R3-ASSIST-001.optionB: Discuss terms from the listing file
RECA-CA-R3-ASSIST-001.optionD: Show the house without discussing price
RECA-CA-R3-ASSIST-001.explanation: DRE permits clerical help at an open house, such as handing out approved information. Showing the property and discussing sale terms require a license.

RECA-CA-R3-AFFILIATE-001.question: A California salesperson holds a current license without a responsible broker. What must happen before negotiating a neighbor's sale for a fee?
RECA-CA-R3-AFFILIATE-001.optionA: Obtain a signed listing directly from the owner
RECA-CA-R3-AFFILIATE-001.optionB: File notice of the proposed sale with DRE
RECA-CA-R3-AFFILIATE-001.optionD: Have the neighbor deposit the fee into escrow
RECA-CA-R3-AFFILIATE-001.explanation: A salesperson must work under a responsible broker to perform licensed acts. Holding a current salesperson license alone does not authorize independent brokerage.

RECA-CA-R3-RECOVERY-002.question: A California buyer holds a qualifying fraud judgment but has made no collection effort. What must precede payment from the Consumer Recovery Account?
RECA-CA-R3-RECOVERY-002.optionA: New arbitration against the same broker
RECA-CA-R3-RECOVERY-002.optionB: A second judgment for the unpaid sum
RECA-CA-R3-RECOVERY-002.optionC: Reasonable efforts to find assets and collect
RECA-CA-R3-RECOVERY-002.optionD: An order permanently revoking the broker's license
RECA-CA-R3-RECOVERY-002.explanation: A qualifying judgment establishes the loss. The claimant must also make a reasonable search for assets and pursue collection from liable, collectible parties.

RECA-CA-R3-DRE-002.question: A California buyer reports a broker's misrepresentation. Which remedy can DRE pursue through its ordinary complaint process?
RECA-CA-R3-DRE-002.optionA: A refund of the buyer's deposit
RECA-CA-R3-DRE-002.explanation: DRE investigates licensing violations and can pursue disciplinary action. A buyer seeking damages or rescission must pursue a separate remedy.

RECA-CA-ADVERT-001.question: In a California real estate team's advertisement, what sets the minimum prominence of the responsible broker's identity?
RECA-CA-ADVERT-001.optionB: Placement of the team leader's license number
RECA-CA-ADVERT-001.optionC: Size of the contact telephone number
RECA-CA-ADVERT-001.explanation: Business and Professions Code 10159.6(b) requires the broker's identity to appear as prominently and conspicuously as the team name.

RECA-CA-R4-ADVANCE-MODIFICATION-STAGES-0.question: A California broker promises a homeowner a residential loan modification and bills for the first stage. When may the broker demand compensation?
RECA-CA-R4-ADVANCE-MODIFICATION-STAGES-0.optionA: When the homeowner signs a fee agreement
RECA-CA-R4-ADVANCE-MODIFICATION-STAGES-0.optionB: When the initial file review is complete
RECA-CA-R4-ADVANCE-MODIFICATION-STAGES-0.optionC: After the lender acknowledges the application
RECA-CA-R4-ADVANCE-MODIFICATION-STAGES-0.explanation: Business and Professions Code 10085.6(a)(1) requires full performance before compensation can be demanded for covered loan modification services. Billing document review as a separate stage does not change that rule.

RECA-CA-R4-ADVANCE-COMPLETED-TASK-001.question: A California broker separately markets a stand-alone listing service under a written limited-service contract. How is payment upon completion classified?
RECA-CA-R4-ADVANCE-COMPLETED-TASK-001.optionC: Advance fee for the eventual sale
RECA-CA-R4-ADVANCE-COMPLETED-TASK-001.explanation: Business and Professions Code 10026(b)(4) excludes payment for qualifying separately marketed tasks under a written limited-service contract once the task is complete. Splitting one larger service into stages does not qualify.

RECA-CA-BUYER-003.question: An individual buyer's California representation agreement renews automatically unless the buyer objects. How must a valid renewal be made?
RECA-CA-BUYER-003.optionA: Through a clause initialed at the original signing
RECA-CA-BUYER-003.optionB: By mutual verbal agreement before expiration
RECA-CA-BUYER-003.optionC: By extending the original agreement in an email from the broker
RECA-CA-BUYER-003.optionD: By dated writing signed by both parties
RECA-CA-BUYER-003.explanation: Civil Code 1670.50 bars automatic renewal. Regulation 2906.1 requires the buyer and broker to sign the renewal before the original agreement expires.

RECA-CA-BUYER-002.question: For an in-person home showing, when does California presume it is practicable for a buyer to sign a representation agreement?
RECA-CA-BUYER-002.optionA: Before the seller accepts the purchase offer
RECA-CA-BUYER-002.optionD: When the buyer submits proof of funds
RECA-CA-BUYER-002.explanation: Regulation 2906.2(a) makes this a rebuttable presumption. The agreement must in any event be signed by the time the buyer executes an offer.

RECA-CA-BUYER-001.question: An individual California buyer signs a representation agreement with no delayed start. How is its maximum three-month term counted?
RECA-CA-BUYER-001.optionA: Three full months from the first day of the following month
RECA-CA-BUYER-001.optionB: Ninety business days starting with the first showing
RECA-CA-BUYER-001.optionC: Ninety calendar days starting the day after the last signature
RECA-CA-BUYER-001.optionD: Three full calendar months from the date of the first offer
RECA-CA-BUYER-001.explanation: Regulation 2906.1 treats three months as 90 calendar days. With no delayed start, day one is the day following the last signature.

RECA-CA-COMP-001.question: Who may pay a California salesperson for negotiating a sale under the salesperson's current license?
RECA-CA-COMP-001.optionB: The seller with the listing broker's consent
RECA-CA-COMP-001.optionC: Either broker named in the purchase contract
RECA-CA-COMP-001.optionD: The buyer under a separate written fee agreement
RECA-CA-COMP-001.explanation: Business and Professions Code 10137 permits compensation for licensed activity only from the broker under whom the salesperson is then licensed.

RENJ-NJ-RG-ENTITY-002.question: A member offers to sign a listing for property held by a New Jersey LLC. What should the broker verify?
RENJ-NJ-RG-ENTITY-002.optionC: Authority to bind the LLC to the listing
RENJ-NJ-RG-ENTITY-002.explanation: Under N.J.S.A. 42:2C-27, membership by itself does not make a person the LLC's agent. The broker needs evidence that the member can act for the owner.

RENJ-NJ-RG-TRUST-002.question: One of two New Jersey co-trustees offers to sign a deed. Which detail in the trust certification matters?
RENJ-NJ-RG-TRUST-002.optionD: Whether either trustee can convey title alone
RENJ-NJ-RG-TRUST-002.explanation: A trust certification can state whether both trustees must act or whether one may sign. The buyer may also request the trust excerpts establishing the trustee's powers.

RENJ-NJ-ATTORNEY-REVIEW-EMAIL-001.question: During New Jersey attorney review, all required recipients receive the seller's attorney's emailed disapproval on time. What follows under Conley?
RENJ-NJ-ATTORNEY-REVIEW-EMAIL-001.optionA: Disapproval is effective upon timely actual notice
RENJ-NJ-ATTORNEY-REVIEW-EMAIL-001.optionD: The buyer must sign a release
RENJ-NJ-ATTORNEY-REVIEW-EMAIL-001.explanation: In Conley v. Guerrero, the buyers received actual notice within the review period. The New Jersey Supreme Court recognized email as an acceptable method of transmitting disapproval.

RENJ-NJ-AGENCY-DISCLOSURE-001.question: A New Jersey broker uses the brokerage services agreement to identify whom the firm represents. Where does that statement belong?
RENJ-NJ-AGENCY-DISCLOSURE-001.optionD: In a separate paragraph titled Agency Disclosure
RENJ-NJ-AGENCY-DISCLOSURE-001.explanation: The agreement must have a separate paragraph titled Agency Disclosure. New Jersey also permits a separate signed writing with that title.

RENJ-NJ-BRANCH-OFFICE-SUPERVISOR-001.question: A New Jersey broker opens a branch. Which employee qualifies to serve as its direct supervisor?
RENJ-NJ-BRANCH-OFFICE-SUPERVISOR-001.optionA: Licensed broker employed as a broker-salesperson
RENJ-NJ-BRANCH-OFFICE-SUPERVISOR-001.optionB: Broker employed by a cooperating firm
RENJ-NJ-BRANCH-OFFICE-SUPERVISOR-001.optionD: Licensed broker serving as an outside adviser
RENJ-NJ-BRANCH-OFFICE-SUPERVISOR-001.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:5-4.5(c) requires a licensed broker employed as a broker-salesperson by the broker maintaining the branch. Sales or management experience alone does not qualify.

RENJ-NJ-BRANCH-IN-DWELLING-001.question: A broker-salesperson proposes a New Jersey branch in their own dwelling with a separate entrance. What may the Commission approve?
RENJ-NJ-BRANCH-IN-DWELLING-001.optionC: Branch if visitors enter by appointment
RENJ-NJ-BRANCH-IN-DWELLING-001.optionD: Branch after an inspection of the separate entrance
RENJ-NJ-BRANCH-IN-DWELLING-001.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:5-4.5(b) bars a branch in the dwelling premises of a salesperson or broker-salesperson. A separate entrance does not remove that restriction.

RENJ-NJ-RG-CONDO-001.question: A New Jersey condo buyer has a building permit to alter a wall. What determines whether association approval is also needed?
RENJ-NJ-RG-CONDO-001.explanation: The master deed, bylaws and applicable rules govern alterations affecting the condominium. A municipal permit addresses public requirements and does not settle the association's authority.

RENJ-NJ-RG-POA-001.question: After a New Jersey owner loses capacity, a durable power authorizes rent collection and payment of property expenses. What can the agent sign?
RENJ-NJ-RG-POA-001.optionB: Check for the building's furnace repair
RENJ-NJ-RG-POA-001.explanation: Durability keeps the granted authority in effect during incapacity. It does not add power to convey or mortgage the property.

RENJ-NJ-RG-POA-003.question: Before signing a deed under a New Jersey durable power of attorney, an agent learns the sole owner died. Who should handle the conveyance?
RENJ-NJ-RG-POA-003.optionB: Agent if the power is recorded
RENJ-NJ-RG-POA-003.optionC: Estate representative with authority to sell
RENJ-NJ-RG-POA-003.explanation: Durability preserves authority during incapacity. Once the agent knows of the principal's death, the good-faith protection for acting without that knowledge does not apply.

RENJ-NJ-RG-POA-002.question: A capable New Jersey owner is overseas. An agent's sale authority takes effect on incapacity. What would authorize the agent to sign now?
RENJ-NJ-RG-POA-002.optionC: Notarized copy of the same power
RENJ-NJ-RG-POA-002.explanation: The capable owner can give the agent current authority. Travel does not satisfy the incapacity condition in the existing power.

RENJ-NJ-RG-LAD-001.question: A New Jersey landlord directs a broker to reject a qualified same-sex couple for their sexual orientation. How should the broker evaluate the application?
RENJ-NJ-RG-LAD-001.optionA: Apply a higher credit threshold set by the owner
RENJ-NJ-RG-LAD-001.optionC: Seek an additional guarantor for this tenancy
RENJ-NJ-RG-LAD-001.optionD: Give preference to otherwise comparable married applicants
RENJ-NJ-RG-LAD-001.explanation: New Jersey's Law Against Discrimination protects sexual orientation in housing. An owner's instruction does not authorize different screening standards.

RENJ-NJ-RG-LAD-002.question: A New Jersey landlord charges a qualified tenant a higher rent because the tenant is transgender. Which provision applies?
RENJ-NJ-RG-LAD-002.explanation: The Law Against Discrimination protects gender identity or expression. Charging a different rent for that reason violates the law even when the landlord offers a lease.

RENJ-NJ-REFERRAL-LICENSE-SERVICE-LIMIT-0.question: A buyer asks a New Jersey referral-company salesperson for help submitting an offer. What may this salesperson do?
RENJ-NJ-REFERRAL-LICENSE-SERVICE-LIMIT-0.optionA: Present the offer to the seller
RENJ-NJ-REFERRAL-LICENSE-SERVICE-LIMIT-0.optionC: Refer the buyer through the employing broker
RENJ-NJ-REFERRAL-LICENSE-SERVICE-LIMIT-0.optionD: Negotiate the price without a fee
RENJ-NJ-REFERRAL-LICENSE-SERVICE-LIMIT-0.explanation: A salesperson licensed with a referral company may send prospects to the broker through whom the salesperson is licensed. That license does not authorize negotiating a purchase.

RENJ-NJ-BUYER-AGREEMENT-001.question: Which New Jersey purchase is exempt from the statutory requirement for a written buyer brokerage services agreement?
RENJ-NJ-BUYER-AGREEMENT-001.explanation: The buyer-agreement requirement applies to residential transactions. New Jersey exempts commercial transactions and treats a single multifamily property with four or fewer units as residential for this purpose.

RENJ-NJ-ATTORNEY-REVIEW-PERIOD-001.question: A New Jersey residential sale contract contains the standard attorney-review clause. Without an extension, how long is review?
RENJ-NJ-ATTORNEY-REVIEW-PERIOD-001.optionD: Until the day of the home inspection
RENJ-NJ-ATTORNEY-REVIEW-PERIOD-001.explanation: The standard period is three business days. Conley v. Guerrero changed the permitted ways to give notice of disapproval and retained the review period.

RENJ-NJ-AGENCY-TERMINATION-001.question: A New Jersey seller and brokerage mutually agree to end their agency relationship early. What makes the termination effective?
RENJ-NJ-AGENCY-TERMINATION-001.optionC: Removal from the multiple listing service
RENJ-NJ-AGENCY-TERMINATION-001.explanation: New Jersey requires written confirmation when the parties end the relationship by mutual agreement. Returning documents or removing a listing does not supply that confirmation.

RENJ-NJ-REBATE-LENDER-NONDISCLOSURE-001.question: A buyer asks a New Jersey broker to conceal a commission rebate from the mortgage lender. Who must receive disclosure?
RENJ-NJ-REBATE-LENDER-NONDISCLOSURE-001.optionD: All transaction parties, including the lender
RENJ-NJ-REBATE-LENDER-NONDISCLOSURE-001.explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16a(a)(3) requires disclosure to every party involved in the transaction, including the mortgage lender. The buyer cannot waive the lender's disclosure.

RE-VAL-026.question: A bank asks a broker to compare recent sales and estimate a foreclosed home's selling price. Which report does the broker prepare?
RE-VAL-026.explanation: A broker price opinion estimates the probable selling price using comparable properties and the broker's judgment. An automated valuation model calculates its estimate from data.

REPA-VAL-026.explanation: A broker price opinion (BPO) is a price estimate a licensee prepares for a lender or other third party, and RELRA section 608.6(e) allows one for a property a lender owns after an unsuccessful foreclosure sale.
